nodes.name: Read email

parameters.query: SELECT id, account_id, subject, participants, platform, confidence, attachments FROM emails WHERE id = $1

nodes.notes: Single row. Every condition test and every downstream action-apply query reads this row via $('Read email').first().json rather than the current item once later nodes fan out to one item per rule.

nodes.name: Read matching rules

parameters.query:
SELECT r.id AS rule_id, r.conditions, r.actions, r.daily_cap, r.condition_summary, r.action_summary,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM rule_runs rr WHERE rr.rule_id = r.id AND rr.ran_at > now() - interval '1 day')::int AS run_count_today
FROM rules r
WHERE r.account_id = $1 AND r.enabled = true

nodes.notes: One row per enabled rule for this email's account, with the daily_cap run-count computed inline (a scalar subquery) rather than a second query -- zero rows here (no enabled rules, or every one already over its cap) means nothing downstream executes for this email at all.

nodes.name: Route by action
nodes.notes: No fallback output -- an actionType of 'Auto-label' (or anything else unrecognized) simply produces no further execution for that item: no email mutation, no rule_runs row, no activity_log row. See Evaluate rule's comment for why.

parameters.query: UPDATE emails SET status = 'archived', handled_at = now(), handled_action = 'archived' WHERE id = $1;

nodes.name: Log Auto-archive activity

parameters.query: INSERT INTO activity_log (account_id, action, target, cause, undoable, undo_payload) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6);

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [$('Read email').first().json.account_id, 'Auto-archive', '"' + $('Read email').first().json.subject + '"', 'Rule: ' + $('Evaluate rule').item.json.conditionSummary, true, JSON.stringify({ table: 'emails', action: 'restore', ids: [$('Evaluate rule').item.json.emailId] })] }}

nodes.notes: undo_payload reuses the exact {table,action,ids} shape lib/data/activity-log.ts already writes for a manual archive (Phase 4) -- POST /api/undo/:actionId handles a rule-driven archive with no new code on the dashboard side.

parameters.query: UPDATE emails SET priority = 'urgent', priority_score = greatest(coalesce(priority_score, 0), 90) WHERE id = $1;
INSERT INTO activity_log (account_id, action, target, cause, undoable, undo_payload) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6);

nodes.name: Call draft webhook
nodes.notes: Calls draft-generation.json's public webhook over HTTP rather than an internal Execute Workflow node -- that workflow's only entry point is its webhook trigger (no Execute Workflow Trigger exists on it), same reasoning gmail-renewal-recovery.json's new resync webhook (Phase 4) used for the opposite direction. Reuses DRAFT_WEBHOOK_SECRET (already required by draft-generation.json itself) -- no new secret. Requires a new SELF_BASE_URL n8n environment variable (this n8n instance's own reachable base URL, e.g. http://localhost:5678) so this workflow can call a sibling webhook on the same instance; tone/length are omitted from the body and default inside draft-generation.json's own Verify secret node (friendly/standard).

parameters.query: INSERT INTO activity_log (account_id, action, target, cause, undoable, undo_payload) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6);

parameters.content:
## Rule Engine

Called non-blocking by triage-pipeline.json right after it writes platform/confidence/priority (this workflow's conditions match on those fields, so it must run after Triage, not in parallel with it like Action/Commitment Extraction).

Single condition, single action per rule -- matches the real capability of app/rules/page.tsx's builder (Phase 4). Auto-label is detected but never applied (no target-category UI exists to collect one). Auto-draft calls draft-generation.json's public webhook over HTTP (requires a new SELF_BASE_URL env var). Auto-archive's activity_log row is undoable (reuses the same undo_payload shape manual archive/done/snooze already write); auto-prioritise and auto-draft are not.

See PHASE-5-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md Wave 1.
